title: Rational highest-weight modules and their integral weights
statement: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional split semisimple Lie algebra over $\mathbf Q$ [def-wf-lie-algebra], [def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra], and let $\mathfrak h$ be a maximal abelian subalgebra acting diagonally in the adjoint representation. Write $R\subset\mathfrak h^\vee$ for its nonzero adjoint weights, $h_\alpha$ for its coroots (the element of $[\mathfrak g_\alpha,\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}]$ on which $\alpha$ takes value $2$), and $\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r\}$ for a simple-root base. Set $P=\{\lambda\in\mathfrak h^\vee:\lambda(h_\alpha)\in\mathbf Z\text{ for every }\alpha\in R\}$. The fundamental weights $\omega_i$, defined by $\omega_i(h_{\alpha_j})=\delta_{ij}$, form a $\mathbf Z$-basis of $P$. For every $\lambda\in P$ with $\lambda(h_{\alpha_i})\ge0$, there exist a nonzero finite-dimensional simple rational representation $L(\lambda)$ and a vector $v_\lambda\ne0$ such that $$h v_\lambda=\lambda(h)v_\lambda,\qquad \mathfrak g_\alpha v_\lambda=0\quad(\alpha\in R^+),$$ where $R^+$ consists of the roots with nonnegative simple-root coordinates. The vectors obtained by finite products of elements of $\mathfrak g$ acting on $v_\lambda$ span $L(\lambda)$ over $\mathbf Q$. There is a direct sum decomposition into ordinary eigenspaces $$L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in\Omega_\lambda}L(\lambda)_\mu,\qquad \Omega_\lambda\subseteq(\lambda-\mathbf Z_{\ge0}\Delta)\cap P,$$ with $\Omega_\lambda$ finite, every displayed space nonzero and $\lambda\in\Omega_\lambda$. The assertions hold over $\mathbf Q$ itself, not merely over its algebraic closure. For $\mathfrak g=0$ the weight $0$ gives $L(0)=\mathbf Q$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-semisimple-root-decomposition] to the given maximal abelian diagonalizing $\mathfrak h$. It supplies the reduced crystallographic root pairing for evaluation, including spanning on both sides. Apply [lem-sfb-root-base-rational-integral-spans] with $V=\mathfrak h^\vee$, $W=\mathfrak h$ and the given $\Delta$: the $h_i=h_{\alpha_i}$ form a rational basis, and every coroot is an integral combination of them. Let $\omega_i$ be the dual rational basis. Then $\xi$ is integral on every coroot if and only if all $\xi(h_i)$ are integers: one direction uses that the $h_i$ are coroots; the other evaluates on their integral combinations. Consequently $P=\bigoplus_i\mathbf Z\omega_i$ by the coordinate identity $\xi=\sum_i\xi(h_i)\omega_i$. Crystallographic integrality also gives $\mathbf Z\Delta\subset P$.

proof.text: Fix a dominant $\lambda\in P$ and write $n_i=\lambda(h_i)\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$. Choose normalized $e_i,f_i$ using [lem-sfb-split-semisimple-root-decomposition]. Construct the explicit rational left-ideal quotient $M=M(\lambda)=U/I_\lambda$ of [lem-sfb-verma-monomial-weight-basis], with generator $v$. Its monomial basis gives $v\ne0$, the ordinary weight decomposition, finite-dimensional weight spaces, weights in $\lambda-\mathbf Z_{\ge0}\Delta$, and $M_\lambda=\mathbf Qv$. This construction uses $\mathbf Q$ throughout, for all dominant integral $\lambda$, including those on walls.

source.place: Printed pp.508 and 511 (rational weight representations required for the Chevalley construction); rational Verma-quotient argument supplied by Q108 (agent), underlying Serre Chapters V-VII WANTED

proof.text: For each $i$ put $w_i=f_i^{n_i+1}v$. It has weight $\nu_i=\lambda-(n_i+1)\alpha_i$. In the associative algebra acting on $M$, expand $[e_i,f_i^m]=\sum_{a=0}^{m-1}f_i^a h_i f_i^{m-1-a}$ and use $h_if_i^bv=(n_i-2b)f_i^bv$. Summing the coefficients gives $e_if_i^mv=m(n_i-m+1)f_i^{m-1}v$, so $e_iw_i=0$. If $j\ne i$, $[e_j,f_i]=0$ gives $e_jw_i=f_i^{n_i+1}e_jv=0$. Since the $e_j$ generate $\mathfrak n^+$ by [lem-sfb-split-semisimple-root-decomposition], all of $\mathfrak n^+$ kills $w_i$.

proof.text: Every $e_i,f_i$ is locally nilpotent on $Q$. Here are the details of propagation from its generator. Fix $x=e_i$ or $f_i$. By [lem-sfb-split-semisimple-root-decomposition], $\operatorname{ad}(x)$ is nilpotent on $\mathfrak g$. It is locally nilpotent on $U$: on a fixed product $y_1\cdots y_d$ its $k$th derivative is a sum of products of derivatives of the $y_j$ of total order $k$, and for large $k$ some factor exceeds its nilpotence bound. This extends to finite linear combinations. Moreover $x\bar v=0$ for $x=e_i$, and $x^{n_i+1}\bar v=0$ for $x=f_i$. For every $u\in U$ the identity $$x^m u\bar v=\sum_{k=0}^m\binom{m}{k}(\operatorname{ad}x)^k(u)x^{m-k}\bar v$$ follows by induction on $m$ from $xu=[x,u]+ux$. If $(\operatorname{ad}x)^a(u)=0$ and $x^b\bar v=0$, take $m\ge a+b$: every summand vanishes since either $k\ge a$ or $m-k\ge b$. Vectors in $Q$ are of the form $u\bar v$ because $M=U v$. This proves local nilpotence without assuming finite-dimensionality of $Q$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-integrable-upper-bounded-weight-finiteness] to $Q$ with the finite set $A=\{\lambda\}$. Step 4 gives the ordinary weight decomposition, finite-dimensional individual weight spaces and the upper cone bound; step 5 gives local nilpotence of every simple raising and lowering operator. The Lie algebra and normalized triples were fixed over $\mathbf Q$ in step 2. All hypotheses of the criterion therefore hold, so $Q$ is finite-dimensional.

source.place: Printed pp.508 and 511 (finite rational highest-weight representations); integrability finiteness input; rational Verma-quotient argument supplied by Q108 (agent), underlying Serre Chapters V-VII WANTED

proof.text: Choose a proper invariant rational subspace $K\subset Q$ of largest dimension (the zero subspace is available and dimensions lie in $\{0,\ldots,\dim Q-1\}$). Then $L=Q/K$ is nonzero and simple: any proper nonzero invariant subspace in it lifts to a proper invariant subspace strictly larger than $K$. The vector $v_\lambda=\bar v+K$ is nonzero since $\bar v$ generates $Q$, and its eigenvalue and positive-root annihilation equations pass to $L$. Its iterated $\mathfrak g$-products span $L$, since $U$ is generated as an algebra by $\mathfrak g$. To verify the ordinary weight decomposition of this quotient, choose $h\in\mathfrak h$ separating the finitely many weights of $Q$. Such an $h$ exists over $\mathbf Q$: the product of their nonzero pairwise differences is a nonzero polynomial, so it is nonzero at some rational point. Lagrange interpolation in the operator $h$ projects onto each weight space. These projections preserve $K$, whence $K=\bigoplus_\mu(K\cap Q_\mu)$ and $L=\bigoplus_\mu Q_\mu/(K\cap Q_\mu)$.

source.place: Printed pp.508 and 511; elementary maximal-dimension quotient and spectral projectors over Q; rational Verma-quotient argument supplied by Q108 (agent), underlying Serre Chapters V-VII WANTED

proof.text: Let $\Omega_\lambda$ be exactly the weights whose quotient spaces in step 7 are nonzero. It is finite because the support of $Q$ is finite. Since $v_\lambda\ne0$, $\lambda\in\Omega_\lambda$, and every displayed eigenspace is nonzero by this choice. Steps 4 and 7 give $\Omega_\lambda\subset\lambda-\mathbf Z_{\ge0}\Delta$. Step 1 gives $\lambda\in P$ and $\mathbf Z\Delta\subset P$, so all these weights lie in $P$. Every algebra, ideal, generator and subspace in the construction was rational, proving the claimed field of definition. Finally, if $\mathfrak g=0$, then $\mathfrak h=0$, $R=\Delta=\varnothing$ and $P=0$; take $L(0)=\mathbf Q$ with the zero action and $v_0=1$. The empty product supplies the spanning vector and the only weight is $0$.
